paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday he sent memes to everyone and invited us out for the weekend, and today he’s like he disappeared. The messages are read, he showed up online, but didn’t reply to a single person. Looks like he’s in zatvor again, so I’m not going to push. When it passes, he’ll show up on his own.

definition_tar_lang: A deliberately hardened ironic tone used online to avoid sounding earnest. Someone with strong '[MASK526]' treats every topic as a joke just to stay unexposed.
sentence_in_context: У него такая [MASK526], что даже про расставание шутит, будто ему вообще всё равно.
sentence_in_context_gloss: His ironic shell is so strong that he even jokes about the breakup, like he doesn't care at all.

definition_tar_lang: An initial burst of hype, irony, or shared mood in a group that makes a meme, joke format, or opinion suddenly rise everywhere. It is the social starter that activates further spread.

definition_tar_lang: A person in a friend group who quietly absorbs everyone's venting, panic, and emotional spillover without making the situation about themselves. They end up saturated with secondhand stress.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday, in our friend group, everyone had something happen at once: one had a deadline, another a breakup, a third a fight with her parents. definition_tar_lang: A lucky but suspiciously specific chain of events that makes an online task work out at the last second, like finding the exact post, person, or screenshot you need. People use it when success feels half-earned and half-magical.
sentence_in_context: Это была чистая [MASK575]: в два клика нашёл тот самый удалённый скрин.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was looking for the author of an old thread with no hope left. definition_tar_lang: A person, persona, or public statement that looks complete at first glance but collapses under one follow-up question. It refers to thin, performative solidity.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday I listened to one “visionary” talk about reforms. While he was reading the slides, everything sounded confident and even polished. definition_tar_lang: To pad out a minor event, skill, or inconvenience with dramatic framing so it sounds like a major saga. It often happens in stories, captions, and self-branding.

definition_tar_lang: The abrupt collective decision to stop discussing a topic online, not because it is resolved, but because everyone senses further talk will only make things worse. The silence feels staged and mutual.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: We argued all day about the new release and it had already gotten into personal digs. Then one person dropped an awkward piece of proof, and a curtain fell over the comments. Nobody convinced anybody; people just abruptly started discussing desktop wallpapers. Very on-brand for us.

definition_tar_lang: A temporary mental blackout during which you read a message, register it, and then instantly lose all memory of it. Often used to explain why someone forgot to reply or missed an obvious detail.
sentence_in_context: У меня утром опять [MASK579]: сообщение прочитал и только вечером вспомнил, что не ответил.

paragraph_in_context: Вчера коллега скинул адрес, где встречаемся, а я даже лайкнул сообщение. Через час уже стоял не у того входа и не понимал, почему все молчат. Классическая [MASK579]: вроде всё видел, а в голове ничего не осталось. Теперь дублирую важное себе в заметки.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday a colleague sent the address of where we were meeting, and I even liked the message. definition_tar_lang: A messy bundle of weak acquaintances, old contacts, and half-dead chats that you keep around just in case you might need something one day. It is your reserve network of possible favors.

Вот за это свою авоську и люблю: выглядит хаосом, а в нужный момент вытаскивает. Главное — не вспоминать о людях только когда прижало.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Before launching the project, I dug through old chats that had been silent since 2019. definition_tar_lang: A private stash of screenshots, links, phrases, and examples collected for a future argument, post, or breakup speech. People build it quietly over time and then open it all at once.
sentence_in_context: У неё на бывшего целая [MASK581]: скрины, даты, ссылки — и всё по папочкам.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: It’s always funny when someone stays quiet for months and then drops a twenty-tweet thread. You can immediately tell the stash wasn’t put together yesterday. The people involved already made up, and the followers forgot, but some still wanted to keep overheating the topic. Every time, someone brings a new "important" reason to be offended. In the end, there's more noise than actual problem.

definition_tar_lang: The low-visibility part of your digital life where abandoned drafts, dead group chats, old accounts, and forgotten projects continue to exist. It is not deleted, just sunk below attention.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: Today I decided to tidy up my phone and got stuck for two hours. In the basement I found old notes, an empty public page, and a chat where nobody had written since last year. I couldn't bring myself to delete everything, so I just renamed a couple of things. sentence_in_context: Опять всё скинули на Машу — она у нас [MASK584], выдержит.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: The chat is quiet again, but I’ve already gotten three urgent requests and someone else’s drama. As if I’m a bucket here that people can endlessly pour everything into. It’s funny that afterward they still ask why I disappear. Probably because even buckets overflow sometimes.

definition_tar_lang: A dense, clumsy chunk of text or audio sent with no structure, usually containing several topics, feelings, and requests at once. You have to cut through it to understand what is wanted.
sentence_in_context: Скинул мне в личку такую буханку, что я минут десять разбирался, что делать.
sentence_in_context_gloss: He sent me such a loaf in DMs that I spent ten minutes figuring out what I was supposed to do.
paragraph_in_context: Обожаю, когда вместо нормального ТЗ прилетает [MASK585] в голосовых и трёх сообщениях подряд. Там и правки, и обиды, и срочная задача, и внезапно мем. Сижу с кофе, собираю из этого хоть какой-то план. Потом ещё оказывается, что главное было в самом конце.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I just love it when, instead of a proper brief, I get a loaf spread across voice notes and three messages in a row. definition_tar_lang: A hidden complication in a seemingly simple plan, usually discovered too late in logistics, relationships, or bureaucracy. The whole thing looked flat until the fold opened up.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: The client wrote in the morning: "It’s all simple there, just pick it up and deliver it." Sure. definition_tar_lang: A person in a group chat or comment thread who blocks momentum by making everyone stop to explain the obvious, clarify context, or wait for them to catch up. Not just slow, but friction-generating.
sentence_in_context: Опять в треде нашлась [MASK587]: полчаса спорим, потому что он не дочитал.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: We got together to quickly decide how to launch the announcement, and we had almost agreed. Then a "plug" jumped in, asked for everything to be explained again from the start, and everything stalled. In the end, instead of publishing by nine, we spent another forty minutes chewing over the same thing. Gotta love such productive calls.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: I went to the office today for the first time in a month and realized I’ve really gone socially stiff. While waiting for the elevator, I wanted to say something to my coworkers twice and froze both times. On Zoom I’m lively and witty, but in person I stand there like an unboxed mannequin. I need to leave the house more often instead of existing only as an avatar.

definition_tar_lang: A small, strategically timed bit of praise, attention, or flirtation used to keep someone engaged without giving them anything substantial. Digital emotional candy.
sentence_in_context: Он опять кинул мне [MASK589] в директ, а на встречу так и не позвал.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: It’s funny how some people know how to keep your interest for months. A like at three in the morning, then a sudden compliment under your story, then “missed you.” But the moment you suggest meeting up, it’s radio silence. Basically, he keeps feeding me little breadcrumbs so I won’t unfollow.

definition_tar_lang: A sprawling private network of weak social ties you only activate when you need a referral, niche information, or a shortcut through bureaucracy. Thin strands, but surprisingly effective.

Кто-то подсказал нормального врача, кто-то свёл с арендодателем без комиссии. В такие моменты понимаешь, что связи решают не только в мемах.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Moving to a new city turned out to be less scary than I thought. At first I didn’t know anyone at all, and then somehow my own web gradually came together. definition_tar_lang: A tiny but oddly decisive detail in someone's profile, post history, or manner of texting that makes you instantly form a strong opinion about them. A fastening point for judgment.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was scrolling through profiles and everything seemed fine. For me, a person can be perfect, but one “good time of day” message and my interest drops sharply.

definition_tar_lang: An atmosphere of vague, sticky agreement in a chat, meeting, or fandom where everyone is being soft and positive but nothing clear, honest, or useful is actually being said.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: I jumped into the discussion of the new season and quickly left. It was such mush there that any normal question immediately drowned in hearts and “oh, let’s keep it positive.” Everyone seems kind, nobody is arguing, but in substance it’s empty. It’s not even clear who actually liked what.

definition_tar_lang: A short, performative public signal of indignation, solidarity, or awareness posted mainly so others can register that you reacted, without any intention of further involvement.
sentence_in_context: Кинул свой [MASK593] в сторис и пошёл дальше по делам.

definition_tar_lang: A person’s carefully arranged stash of screenshots, links, memes, and references kept ready to be pulled out in chats to seem witty, informed, or emotionally articulate.

Everything there is sorted into folders: reactions, old tweets, useful quotes, and one killer meme for emergencies. Yesterday it worked again: he wrote “I see,” and I already had the perfect reply. definition_tar_lang: To make your online presence look polished and untouchable right after an embarrassing episode, as if everything has always been clean, calm, and under control.
sentence_in_context: После вчерашнего фейла она за час застеклила профиль, будто ничего и не было.
sentence_in_context_gloss: After yesterday’s fail, she polished up her profile in an hour as if nothing had happened.
paragraph_in_context: Ночью у него был какой-то дикий срыв в сторис, все это видели. Утром захожу — лента идеальная, новые фото, спокойные подписи, комментарии подчищены. Прямо взял и застеклил весь аккаунт за пару часов. Теперь выглядит так, будто он всегда был самым собранным человеком в интернете.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: At night he had some wild meltdown in his stories, and everyone saw it. In the morning I check — the feed is perfect, new photos, calm captions, comments cleaned up. He basically went and glazed over the whole account in a couple of hours. Now it looks like he was always the most composed person on the internet.

definition_tar_lang: A conspicuously wholesome post or public statement dropped to cover over recent mess, backlash, cringe, or suspicious behavior without directly addressing it.
sentence_in_context: После вчерашнего скандала их внезапный пост про котиков выглядел как чистая [MASK596].
sentence_in_context_gloss: After yesterday’s scandal, their sudden post about kittens looked like pure whitewashing.
paragraph_in_context: Бренд весь день молчал, пока в комментах их разносили за рекламу. А потом выкатили милую сторис про «добро и заботу», будто ничего не было. Такая [MASK596] только сильнее бесит, если честно. Лучше бы нормально извинились и ответили по делу.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The brand stayed silent all day while people were tearing them apart in the comments over the ad. And then they rolled out a cute story about “kindness and care,” as if nothing had happened. That kind of whitewashing just makes people even more annoyed, honestly. They should have apologized properly and addressed the issue directly.

definition_tar_lang: A brain state in which every task, tab, message, and intention immediately slips away, especially after doomscrolling or context-switching all day.
sentence_in_context: После трёх созвонов и часа в ленте у меня в голове полное [MASK597].
sentence_in_context_gloss: After three calls and an hour in the feed, my head is a complete sieve.
paragraph_in_context: С утра открыл рабочий чат на минуту и пропал в ссылках, мемах и чужих задачах. К обеду поймал какое-то [MASK597]: зашёл написать письмо, а через пять минут уже искал, где потерял мысль. Пойду выключу уведомления и хотя бы одну задачу доведу до конца. Иначе этот день меня добьёт.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: In the morning I opened the work chat for a minute and disappeared into links, memes, and other people’s tasks. By lunch I’d hit some kind of sieve-state: I went in to write an email, and five minutes later I was already trying to remember where I’d lost the thought. I’m going to turn off notifications and at least finish one task. Otherwise this day will finish me off.

definition_tar_lang: To aggressively trim a story, opinion, or memory into a neat, dramatic version fit for posting, leaving out all the awkward or complicating parts.
sentence_in_context: Опять начал [MASK598] нашу поездку под героическую историю, будто мы вообще не ругались.
sentence_in_context_gloss: He started trimming our trip into a heroic story again, as if we never argued at all.
paragraph_in_context: Заметила, как мы все начали [MASK598] воспоминания под удобный формат для сторис. Вчерашний вечер уже выглядит как идеальный спонтанный праздник, хотя половину времени мы мерзли и искали, где зарядить телефон. Через неделю, чувствую, останется только «лучшая ночь этого лета». Интернет реально шлифует память.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I noticed how we’ve all started trimming our memories into a convenient format for stories. Last night already looks like a perfect spontaneous celebration, even though we spent half the time freezing and looking for a place to charge a phone. In a week, I feel like only “the best night of this summer” will remain. The internet really polishes memory.

definition_tar_lang: A fake practical excuse someone wears over their actual motive when joining a conversation, event, or group chat they mainly entered to watch drama unfold.
sentence_in_context: Зашёл в чат якобы за ссылкой, но этот [MASK599] слетел после третьего сообщения.
sentence_in_context_gloss: He joined the chat supposedly for a link, but that cover story fell apart after the third message.
paragraph_in_context: Коллега внезапно появился на созвоне и сказал, что ему нужен один файл. Мы уже переглянулись, потому что вчера он вообще не интересовался проектом. Через пять минут стало ясно, что файл был просто [MASK599]ом. Он сидел молча и ждал, когда начнётся разбор ссоры между отделами.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: A coworker suddenly showed up on the call and said he needed one file. We exchanged looks already, because yesterday he had shown no interest in the project at all. Five minutes later it became clear that the file was just a cover story. He sat there silently, waiting for the argument between departments to begin.

definition_tar_lang: A dead group chat, channel, or social feed where posts are technically still being made but all emotion, spontaneity, and actual interaction have evaporated.
sentence_in_context: Наш бывший ламповый чат окончательно превратился в сушилку: одни дежурные реакции.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Our once cozy chat has finally turned into a dryer: nothing but perfunctory reactions.
paragraph_in_context: Зашёл сегодня в канал факультета — там опять три поста по расписанию и ноль живых комментариев. Раньше хоть спорили, шутили, кидали мемы между объявлениями. Сейчас это какая-то [MASK600] с автопилотом вместо людей. Даже странно, что уведомления ещё приходят.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I checked the faculty channel today—again, three scheduled posts and zero real comments. It used to have arguments, jokes, and memes between announcements. Now it’s some kind of dryer, with autopilot instead of people. It’s strange that notifications still even come in.

definition_tar_lang: A person who cannot consume anything online without drifting into endless feed-scrolling. They open the phone for one task and vanish into the stream for half an hour.
sentence_in_context: Зашёл ответить в чат на минутку и опять как [MASK601] пропал до ночи.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I popped into the chat to reply for a minute and again vanished like a doom-scroller until late at night.
paragraph_in_context: Хотела быстро проверить погоду перед выходом. Через сорок минут уже смотрю чужие ремонты, мемы и обзоры кружек. Всё, официально признаю: я [MASK601] с большим стажем. Телефон надо класть в другую комнату, иначе день снова куда-то исчезает.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I just wanted to quickly check the weather before going out. Forty minutes later I’m already watching other people’s renovations, memes, and mug reviews. That’s it, I officially admit it: I’m a chronic scroll-addict. I need to leave my phone in another room, otherwise the day disappears again.

definition_tar_lang: The useless ritual of reopening, refreshing, and staring at a lagging page that keeps flashing signs of life but never fully loads. It is the whole stubborn interaction, not the glitch itself.
sentence_in_context: С утра одно [MASK602] с госуслугами: обновляю, жду, а запись к врачу так и не открывается.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Since morning it’s been nothing but morgalovo with the public services site: I refresh, wait, and the doctor appointment page still won’t open.
paragraph_in_context: Пытался купить билеты на концерт в обеденный перерыв. Сайт вроде оживает, потом снова висит, и начинается привычное [MASK602]. Обновил страницу раз двадцать, даже капчу успел возненавидеть. В итоге места разобрали быстрее, чем у меня что-то загрузилось.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I tried to buy concert tickets during my lunch break. The site seems to come alive, then freezes again, and the usual morgalovo starts. I refreshed the page about twenty times and even managed to start hating the captcha. In the end, the seats were snapped up faster than anything loaded for me.

definition_tar_lang: A person who is always invisibly active in group chats, channels, and shared docs, somehow shaping everything without drawing attention. They are not loud, just endlessly and suspiciously present.
sentence_in_context: Пока все молчали, наш [MASK603] уже поправил таблицу, дедлайны и описание канала.
sentence_in_context_gloss: While everyone stayed silent, our shurshak had already fixed the spreadsheet, deadlines, and the channel description.
paragraph_in_context: В чате снова никто ничего не обсуждал вслух, но к утру всё как-то собралось. Ссылки на месте, созвон перенесён, в документе исчезли странные правки. Я уже не удивляюсь: у нас в команде есть один [MASK603]. Его как будто не видно, но следы везде.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Again, nobody discussed anything out loud in the chat, but by morning everything had somehow come together. The links were in place, the call was rescheduled, and the strange edits in the document were gone. I’m not surprised anymore: our team has a shurshak. You barely notice him, but his traces are everywhere.

definition_tar_lang: The tiny but infuriating moment when a video, voice call, or stream drops just enough quality to make meaning feel slippery. It is not a full crash, just a brief smear that breaks comprehension.
sentence_in_context: На созвоне опять словил пару [MASK604], и половину шутки начальника не понял.
sentence_in_context_gloss: On the call I caught a couple of smudges again, and didn't understand half of the boss's joke.
paragraph_in_context: Смотрели матч всей компанией в дискорде, и интернет как назло начал чудить. Картинка нормальная, звук тоже вроде идёт, а потом вдруг несколько [MASK604] подряд — и уже неясно, кто забил и что орёт комментатор. Самое бесячее, что через секунду всё снова идеально. Будто связь специально издевается.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: We were watching the match together in Discord, and the internet started acting up at the worst possible time. The picture was fine, the sound seemed okay too, and then suddenly several smudges in a row—and it was no longer clear who scored or what the commentator was yelling. The most annoying part is that a second later everything is perfect again. It's like the connection is messing with you on purpose.

definition_tar_lang: The annoying cycle where a notification badge, cursor, or tab keeps flashing for attention and drags your eyes back to it. It refers less to one blink than to the whole low-grade harassment pattern.
sentence_in_context: Выключил все баннеры, а это [MASK605] в вкладке всё равно не даёт сосредоточиться.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I turned off all the banners, but that flashing nuisance in the tab still won’t let me concentrate.
paragraph_in_context: Сел спокойно дописать отчёт, и тут опять началось это [MASK605] в рабочем чате. Один красный кружок исчезает, второй тут же вылезает, курсор дёргается, вкладка мигает. Вроде мелочь, а через десять минут уже бесит сильнее самой задачи. Поймал себя на том, что просто жду тишины от экрана.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I sat down to calmly finish the report, and then that flashing nuisance started up again in the work chat. One red dot disappears, a second one pops up right away, the cursor twitches, the tab flashes. It seems like a small thing, but after ten minutes it’s already more annoying than the task itself. I caught myself just waiting for the screen to finally go quiet.

definition_tar_lang: The habit of instantly clearing notifications, reminders, or pop-ups without reading them, just to restore visual calm. It names the whole reflexive swipe-away routine, not a single gesture.
sentence_in_context: Опять на автомате устроила смахню и только потом заметила пропущенный звонок.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Again I did my usual swipe-away routine on autopilot and only then noticed the missed call.
paragraph_in_context: Утро началось как всегда: будильник, три напоминания, какая-то акция от банка. Я спросонья включила свою смахню и расчистила экран за две секунды. Через час выяснилось, что среди этого всего было сообщение от врача. Ну вот почему мозг считает, что всё всплывающее — это шум?
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The morning started as usual: alarm, three reminders, some promo from the bank. Half-asleep, I switched on my usual swipe-away routine and cleared the screen in two seconds. An hour later it turned out that among all that there had been a message from my doctor. Why does my brain think that everything popping up is just noise?

definition_tar_lang: The group-chat condition where everyone keeps politely agreeing, reacting, and saying 'yeah' but nobody actually takes action. It is consensus without momentum.
sentence_in_context: У нас в чате опять [MASK607]: все за, а дедлайн уже второй день горит.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Our chat is doing the nod-fest again: everyone’s on board, but the deadline has already been burning for the second day.
paragraph_in_context: Созвонились, обсудили идеи, накидали реакций под сообщением. Потом начался привычный [MASK607]: «да-да», «супер», «поддерживаю». Через час тишина, никто даже файл не открыл. Люблю наши продуктивные понедельники.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: We got on a call, discussed ideas, and dropped reactions under the message. Then the usual nod-fest started: “yeah-yeah,” “great,” “I support it.” An hour later, silence — no one had even opened the file. Gotta love our productive Mondays.

definition_tar_lang: A person who tags everyone into every minor update, meme, or side thought as if all moments require a summons. The term implies exhausting over-inclusion.
sentence_in_context: Опять этот [MASK608] отметил весь чат из-за фотки кофе, ну сколько можно.
sentence_in_context_gloss: That tag maniac tagged the whole chat again because of a coffee photo, how much longer can this go on?
paragraph_in_context: У нас в рабочем чате завёлся настоящий [MASK608]. Любую мелочь превращает в общий сбор: стикер кинул, мем нашёл, лампочка у него мигнула — и всем летят отметки. Уже боюсь открывать уведомления по утрам. Скоро начну отвечать только после обеда, чтобы не сгореть.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: A real tag maniac has appeared in our work chat. He turns every little thing into a full-group summons: he posts a sticker, finds a meme, his light bulb flickers—and everyone gets tagged. I'm already afraid to open notifications in the morning. Soon I'll start replying only after lunch so I don't burn out.

definition_tar_lang: Fast, almost panicky scanning through posts, photos, or messages to create the illusion that you've 'caught up.' It emphasizes motion and input without retention.
sentence_in_context: С утра устроил дикий [MASK609] чатов и к обеду уже ничего не помню.
sentence_in_context_gloss: In the morning I did a wild frantic scroll through chats, and by lunch I already remembered nothing.
paragraph_in_context: Пять минут без телефона, и там уже сорок новых сообщений. Захожу с мыслью «сейчас быстро разберусь», но получается один сплошной [MASK609]. Вроде всё посмотрел, всем поставил реакции, а что было важное — вообще мимо. Потом ещё полдня собираю по кускам, кто о чём писал.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Five minutes without my phone, and there are already forty new messages. I go in thinking, "I'll sort it out quickly now," but it turns into one continuous frantic scroll. It feels like I looked at everything and reacted to everyone, but whatever was important completely passed me by. Then I spend half the day piecing together who wrote about what.

definition_tar_lang: The oddly wholesome energy of friends slowly assembling in a chat, lobby, or call, with fragments of greetings, test messages, and small jokes before anything begins. It names the pre-event togetherness itself.
sentence_in_context: Обожаю эту сбороту перед стримом: кто-то шуршит микрофоном, кто-то кидает мемы.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I love this sborota before the stream: someone is rustling their microphone, someone else is posting memes.
paragraph_in_context: До фильма оставалось минут десять, и в голосовом уже началась [MASK610]. Один зашёл и сказал только «алло», второй молча включил камеру с котом, остальные подтягивались с чаем и шутками. В такие моменты даже не важно, что именно будем смотреть.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: There were about ten minutes left before the movie, and the sborota had already started in voice chat. One person joined and only said “hello,” another silently turned on their camera with a cat, and the rest trickled in with tea and jokes. In moments like that, it doesn’t even matter what exactly we’re going to watch.

definition_tar_lang: The mode where you keep your online status invisible, avoid replying, and watch everything from the shadows for days. Not total absence, but deliberate low-visibility existence.
sentence_in_context: Я второй день в [MASK611]е: сторис смотрю, а в чаты вообще не захожу.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I've been in hiding mode for the second day: I watch stories, but I don't go into chats at all.
paragraph_in_context: После этой недели хочется просто уйти в [MASK611]. Уведомления выключил, статус спрятал, но ленту всё равно листаю перед сном. Если что-то срочное, лучше звоните, потому что в мессенджерах я сейчас как призрак. Пару дней так побуду и вернусь в нормальный режим.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: After this week, I just want to go into hiding mode. I turned off notifications and hid my status, but I still scroll the feed before bed. If it's urgent, it's better to call, because in messengers I'm basically like a ghost right now. I'll stay like this for a couple of days and then return to normal mode.

definition_tar_lang: The irritating phase when every tap or click opens another tiny menu, pop-up, or layer instead of doing the one thing you wanted. A feeling of being pecked to death by interface micro-actions.
sentence_in_context: Обновил приложение, и опять началась [MASK612]: чтобы оплатить, прошёл семь экранов.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I updated the app, and the click-plague started again: to pay, I had to go through seven screens.
paragraph_in_context: Хотел быстро заказать кофе по дороге, а словил какую-то щелкуху в приложении. Нажимаю на корзину — вылезает подсказка, потом окно с акцией, потом ещё выбор способа оплаты поверх выбора адреса. За минуту сделал двадцать тапов и так и не оформил заказ. Иногда интерфейсы будто специально проверяют терпение.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I wanted to quickly order coffee on the way, but ran into some kind of click-plague in the app. I tap the cart—and a tip pops up, then a promo window, then yet another payment method choice on top of the address selection. In a minute I made twenty taps and still didn’t place the order. Sometimes interfaces seem like they’re deliberately testing your patience.

definition_tar_lang: The state of consuming short posts, clips, or notifications in a continuous stream without remembering any individual item afterward. It feels like feeding on content rather than engaging with it.
sentence_in_context: Весь вечер опять ушёл в [MASK613]: листал ленту, а что видел — уже не помню.
sentence_in_context_gloss: The whole evening disappeared into glotnyak again: I scrolled the feed, and I already don’t remember what I saw.
paragraph_in_context: Сел на пять минут проверить сообщения перед сном. Очнулся через час: сторис, рилсы, мемы, какие-то новости подряд. Самый чистый [MASK613] — вроде постоянно что-то смотришь, а в голове пусто. Надо хотя бы телефон оставлять в другой комнате.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I sat down to check messages for five minutes before bed. I came to an hour later: stories, reels, memes, some kind of news one after another. The purest glotnyak — it feels like you’re constantly watching something, but your head stays empty. I need to at least leave my phone in another room.

definition_tar_lang: The annoying half-loading behavior where content appears in drips and fragments, making you keep waiting and checking whether the page is finally done. Not a full freeze, but death by incremental loading.
sentence_in_context: Опять этот [MASK614] в приложении: уже всё открыл, а фотки доползают по одной.
sentence_in_context_gloss: That annoying half-loading again in the app: everything’s already open, but the photos crawl in one by one.
paragraph_in_context: Сел быстро посмотреть отзывы перед заказом, и начался [MASK614]. Текст уже на экране, потом через паузу появляются аватарки, потом ещё картинки. Сидишь и не понимаешь, то ли всё прогрузилось, то ли сейчас ещё что-нибудь вылезет. Вроде не виснет, но бесит сильнее.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I sat down to quickly check reviews before ordering, and then the half-loading started. The text is already on the screen, then after a pause the avatars appear, then more images. You sit there not knowing whether everything has finished loading or if something else is still about to pop in. It’s not exactly frozen, but it’s even more annoying.

definition_tar_lang: The oddly cozy feeling of seeing the same joke format, opinion, or phrase bounce around your feed from person to person all day. Repetitive, but socially reassuring in a faintly ridiculous way.
sentence_in_context: К вечеру лента превратилась в сплошную эхоту, и почему-то стало даже уютнее.
sentence_in_context_gloss: By evening my feed had turned into one continuous ekhota, and somehow it even felt cozier.
paragraph_in_context: С утра увидел один и тот же мем у трёх разных людей, потом ещё в рабочих чатах. Обычно такое раздражает, а сегодня поймал себя на странном спокойствии. Какая-то [MASK615] накрыла ленту, будто все сидим в одной комнате и хихикаем над одним и тем же. Немного глупо, но приятно.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: In the morning I saw the same meme from three different people, then again in work chats. Usually that kind of thing annoys me, but today I caught myself feeling strangely calm. Some kind of ekhota washed over my feed, as if we were all sitting in one room giggling at the same thing. A little silly, but nice.

definition_tar_lang: A person who never reads menus, labels, or settings and just pokes the screen until something happens. Their style is not exploration but blind kinetic improvisation.
sentence_in_context: Опять наш [MASK616] в приложении всё сбил, даже будильник на 3:17 поставил.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Our button-masher messed everything up in the app again, even set the alarm for 3:17.
paragraph_in_context: Дал папе новый смартфон, думал, быстро освоится. Но он как [MASK616]: за минуту включил авиарежим, убрал звук и потерял фонарик. Потом сказал, что телефон «сырой» и ничего не понятно. Сижу теперь возвращаю всё обратно.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I gave my dad a new smartphone, thinking he’d get the hang of it quickly. But he’s such a button-masher: in a minute he turned on airplane mode, muted the sound, and somehow lost the flashlight. Then he said the phone was “unfinished” and nothing made sense. Now I’m sitting here putting everything back.

definition_tar_lang: The restless condition when too many chats, alerts, and half-formed thoughts are simmering in your head at once, so you keep opening apps without doing anything useful. It feels like your attention is quietly boiling over.
sentence_in_context: С утра какой-то [MASK617]: прыгаю между чатами, а к задаче так и не сел.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Since morning it’s been some kind of bulnyak: I’m jumping between chats, but still haven’t sat down to the task.

paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was trying to pay for an order with my phone at the checkout, and some kind of flicker-mess started. The internet icon kept appearing and disappearing, the bank was blasting notifications in batches, and the terminal was beeping. In the end everyone was looking at me like I was stalling on purpose. Love it when technology adds drama out of nowhere.

definition_tar_lang: A restless state where you keep hopping to whatever next thing gives an instant tiny reward: one more tab, one more clip, one more alert, one more idea. It is attention fragmentation powered by mini-clicks of novelty.
sentence_in_context: Сел дописать отчёт, а через десять минут снова поймал себя на [MASK686]е.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I sat down to finish the report, and ten minutes later caught myself in that click-chasing restless mode again.
paragraph_in_context: Хотел спокойно почитать перед сном, но вечер опять развалился. Открыл одно сообщение, потом зачем-то полез смотреть погоду, потом рилсы, потом чужой канал. В итоге час прошёл, а в голове только [MASK686] и ощущение, что мозг весь день бегал без остановки. Надо хотя бы уведомления ночью рубить.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I wanted to read calmly before bed, but the evening fell apart again. I opened one message, then for some reason checked the weather, then reels, then someone else’s channel. In the end, an hour passed, and all that was left in my head was that clicky restless mode and the feeling that my brain had been running all day without stopping. At least I need to turn notifications off at night.

definition_tar_lang: The whole irritating pattern of messages, calls, uploads, or thoughts getting interrupted at the exact point where meaning was about to become clear. It refers less to one break than to the cumulative experience of repeated cutoffs.
sentence_in_context: Опять эта [MASK687]: созвон завис, файл не отправился, и мысль уже уплыла.
sentence_in_context_gloss: That damn obryvnya again: the call froze, the file didn’t send, and the thought already drifted away.
paragraph_in_context: С утра всё шло нормально, пока не началась какая-то [MASK687]. Пишу одно сообщение — приложение вылетает, перезваниваю — связь рвётся на самом важном месте. Потом ещё и черновик поста исчез. К вечеру уже не злюсь, просто смешно, насколько день решил меня не договорить.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Everything was going fine in the morning until some kind of obryvnya started. I type one message and the app crashes; I call back and the connection drops at the most important moment. Then even the draft of my post disappeared. By evening I’m not even angry anymore, it’s just funny how determined the day was not to let me finish anything.

definition_tar_lang: Someone who is constantly active behind the scenes in a chat, server, or shared workspace, tweaking little things, resurfacing old links, adjusting details, and generating a sense of perpetual minor motion. They are useful, but exhausting to track.
sentence_in_context: Опять наш [MASK688] ночью переименовал каналы и поднял древний гуглодок.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Our busy little behind-the-scenes person renamed the channels again at night and brought up an ancient Google Doc.
paragraph_in_context: Зашёл утром в рабочий чат, а там уже всё немного не так. Ссылки обновлены, закреп поменян, старый тред снова наверху. Похоже, наш [MASK688] не спал и тихо навёл свою странную «косметику». Полезно, конечно, но пока поймёшь, что именно изменилось, уже устанешь.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I logged into the work chat in the morning, and everything was already slightly different. The links were updated, the pinned message had been changed, and an old thread was back at the top. Looks like our behind-the-scenes fidgeter didn’t sleep and quietly did their strange “cosmetic” tweaks. Useful, sure, but by the time you figure out what exactly changed, you’re already tired.

definition_tar_lang: That low-grade, drizzly mood of a chat or feed where nothing important happens, but people keep posting small, grey little updates. Somehow boring and cozy at the same time.
sentence_in_context: В чате с утра такая [MASK689]: мемы, кофе, коты, и никто никуда не спешит.
sentence_in_context_gloss: The chat has had such a drizzly mood since morning: memes, coffee, cats, and nobody is rushing anywhere.
paragraph_in_context: Лента сегодня совсем без новостей, зато уютная. Кто-то выложил дождь за окном, кто-то — кривой капучино, потом пошли сонные селфи и фото носков. Люблю такую моросоту по средам: ничего важного, но закрывать приложение не хочется.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The feed has no news at all today, but it’s cozy. Someone posted the rain outside the window, someone else a lopsided cappuccino, then sleepy selfies and photos of socks started appearing. I love this kind of drizzly mood on Wednesdays: nothing important, but you don’t want to close the app.

definition_tar_lang: The pointless process of dragging windows, tabs, or files around the screen without actually deciding anything. It usually happens when someone wants to feel busy instead of choosing.
sentence_in_context: Полчаса шаркни в браузере, а отчёт как был не начат, так и остался.
sentence_in_context_gloss: Half an hour of sharknya in the browser, and the report still remained as unstarted as before.
paragraph_in_context: Сел работать над презентацией ещё утром. Через час поймал себя на шаркне между вкладками, папками и окнами, будто от этого слайды сами соберутся. Самое смешное — устал, как после нормальной работы. А по факту готов только заголовок.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I sat down to work on the presentation back in the morning. An hour later I caught myself doing sharknya between tabs, folders, and windows, as if the slides would assemble themselves from that. The funniest part is that I got tired as if I’d done real work. But in fact, only the title is ready.

definition_tar_lang: A person who instantly bites on every provocative post, teaser, or fake announcement. They are easy to hook not because they're naive, but because they can't resist reacting first.
sentence_in_context: Опять влетел в комменты с пеной у рта — ну ты и [MASK691].
sentence_in_context_gloss: You jumped into the comments foaming at the mouth again — you’re such a klyuvyak.
paragraph_in_context: Админ ночью вбросил странный тизер про «закрытие проекта», и понеслось. Пока все ждали деталей, один [MASK691] уже накатал десять гневных сообщений и собрал пол-канала. Утром выяснилось, что это был анонс обновления. Но шоу он, конечно, сделал знатное.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: The admin dropped a weird teaser at night about the “project shutting down,” and off it went. While everyone else was waiting for details, one klyuvyak had already written ten angry messages and dragged half the channel into it. By morning it turned out to be an update announcement. But he definitely put on quite a show.

definition_tar_lang: A tiny, almost invisible sign that someone is active online—an avatar twitch, a status flicker, a typing hint that appears and vanishes. Too little to count as contact, but enough to keep you watching.
sentence_in_context: Опять ловлю этот [MASK692] в чате и зачем-то не могу закрыть приложение.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I keep catching that shurkhok in the chat again, and for some reason I can't close the app.
paragraph_in_context: Смешно, как один [MASK692] может испортить весь вечер. Уже решила не проверять мессенджер, но там то кружок мелькнёт, то статус мигнёт. Ничего не происходит, а внимание всё равно туда уезжает. Похоже, пора уже выключать уведомления и себя тоже.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: It’s funny how one shurkhok can ruin the whole evening. I’d already decided not to check the messenger, but then the little circle flashes, or the status blinks. Nothing is actually happening, yet my attention keeps drifting there anyway. Looks like it’s time to turn off notifications—and maybe myself too.

definition_tar_lang: The suspicious, overfocused state when you're rereading a message trying to detect hidden tone, passive aggression, or subtext. The words stay the same, but your trust keeps shrinking.
sentence_in_context: После его «ок, как хочешь» у меня включился [MASK693], и вечер пропал.
sentence_in_context_gloss: After his “ok, as you want,” I went into shchurnyak mode, and the whole evening was ruined.
paragraph_in_context: Ненавижу переписки после ссоры. Читаешь обычное «понятно» и сразу ловишь [MASK693], будто там между буквами спрятан упрёк. Потом десять минут смотришь на точку в конце сообщения и придумываешь драму. Вживую бы за две секунды всё стало ясно.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I hate texting after an argument. You read a simple “got it” and instantly get shchurnyak, like there’s a reproach hidden between the letters. Then you spend ten minutes staring at the period at the end of the message and inventing drama. In person, everything would become clear in two seconds.

definition_tar_lang: A person who keeps dropping shiny but low-substance updates just to stay visible in the feed. Each post rings briefly, attracts eyes, and leaves nothing behind.
sentence_in_context: Опять этот [MASK694] выкатил сторис ни о чём, лишь бы напомнить о себе.
sentence_in_context_gloss: That flashy poser posted another meaningless story again, just to remind everyone he exists.
paragraph_in_context: Подписался на него из-за пары толковых разборов, а дальше пошёл сплошной шум. Сегодня мем, завтра селфи, послезавтра загадочный анонс без продолжения. В ленте мелькает постоянно, но пользы ноль. Настоящий [MASK694], если честно.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I followed him because of a couple of solid breakdowns, but after that it was just nonstop noise. Today a meme, tomorrow a selfie, the day after a mysterious announcement with no follow-up. He keeps popping up in the feed, but there’s zero value. A real brynyak, honestly.

definition_tar_lang: The humiliating ritual of scraping together enough words, screenshots, or evidence to make a weak online point sound solid. It suggests visible effort with unimpressive results.
sentence_in_context: Опять устроил [MASK695] в комментах: десять скринов, а аргумент всё равно никакой.
sentence_in_context_gloss: He pulled that skreblovo again in the comments: ten screenshots, and the argument is still worthless.
paragraph_in_context: Вчера один тип весь вечер доказывал, что не врал. Притащил старые переписки, кривые скрины и какие-то обрезанные ссылки. Смотрелось это как чистое [MASK695], если честно. Чем больше он старался, тем слабее выглядел.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday some guy spent the whole evening trying to prove he wasn’t lying. He dragged in old chats, crooked screenshots, and some cropped links. Honestly, it looked like pure skreblovo. The harder he tried, the weaker he looked.

definition_tar_lang: A screenshot, meme, or repost that has been compressed, cropped, captioned, and re-saved so many times it becomes visually grimy. Everyone still shares it, even though it looks digitally handled to death.
sentence_in_context: Опять кинули этот [MASK696] в чат — пиксели уже громче шутки.
sentence_in_context_gloss: They dropped that murzyak in the chat again — the pixels are louder than the joke now.
paragraph_in_context: Искал исходник мема для сторис, а нашёл только какой-то [MASK696] из 2018-го. Сверху чужая подпись, снизу обрезанный логотип, всё мыльное и пережатое. Но самое смешное, что именно эту версию все и пересылают. Видимо, у нормального качества просто нет шансов.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I was looking for the original meme for my story, but all I found was some murzyak from 2018. Someone else’s caption is on top, a cropped logo is at the bottom, and everything is blurry and over-compressed. But the funniest part is that this is exactly the version everyone keeps forwarding. Apparently normal quality just doesn’t stand a chance.

definition_tar_lang: The gradual draining of enthusiasm in a chat, stream, or collaborative plan while nobody officially leaves. You can feel the energy souring in real time.
sentence_in_context: Сначала все орали идеи в чат, а потом какой-то [MASK697] и тишина до утра.
sentence_in_context_gloss: At first everyone was shouting ideas in the chat, and then some kind of kisyozh and silence until morning.
paragraph_in_context: Вчера собирались быстро добить совместный проект, даже созвон открыли без опозданий. Первые двадцать минут вообще летели: шутки, ссылки, наброски. А потом начался [MASK697] — никто не отвалился, но ответы стали редкими и какими-то вялыми. В итоге вроде все были онлайн, а дело встало намертво.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday we were going to quickly finish a collaborative project, and we even started the call without anyone being late. The first twenty minutes really flew by: jokes, links, sketches. And then kisyozh started—no one dropped off, but the replies became sparse and kind of limp. In the end, everyone was technically online, but the work came to a complete standstill.

definition_tar_lang: That oddly enjoyable comment-thread atmosphere when an argument is clearly pointless but entertaining enough that everyone keeps reading. It is conflict experienced as ambient spectacle.
sentence_in_context: Зашёл на пять минут, а там такая [MASK698], что залип до полуночи.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I dropped in for five minutes, but it was such a glorious mess that I got stuck there until midnight.
paragraph_in_context: Хотел лечь спать пораньше, но открыл комменты под новостью про редизайн. Там уже третий час идёт [MASK698]: одни требуют вернуть старую кнопку, другие спорят из принципа. Сам ничего не пишу, просто обновляю страницу и читаю. Это ужасно, конечно, но почему-то невозможно оторваться.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: I wanted to go to bed early, but I opened the comments under a news post about the redesign. There’s been this ongoing mess for the third hour already: some are demanding the old button back, others are arguing out of principle. I’m not even writing anything myself, just refreshing the page and reading. It’s terrible, of course, but somehow impossible to look away.

definition_tar_lang: All the little frantic online actions around a deadline—renaming files, reposting links, pinging people, opening documents—that create activity without solving the actual problem. It is digital bustle mistaken for progress.
sentence_in_context: За час до сдачи началась привычная [MASK699]: чаты ожили, а презентация всё ещё пустая.
sentence_in_context_gloss: An hour before the deadline, the usual shurnya started: the chats came alive, but the presentation was still empty.
paragraph_in_context: Вчера весь отдел с утра был в шурне. Кто-то срочно переименовывал файлы, кто-то кидал новые ссылки, кто-то писал «уже почти готово». К вечеру стало тихо и неловко. Оказалось, что сам отчёт никто так и не собрал.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Yesterday the whole department had been in shurnya since morning. Someone was urgently renaming files, someone was sending new links, someone was writing “it’s almost ready.” By evening it got quiet and awkward. It turned out that no one had actually put the report together.

definition_tar_lang: The stale after-feeling left by a half-finished online project, abandoned draft, or dead chat that nobody formally closed. It lingers as low-level guilt and unfinished business.
sentence_in_context: Открыл старый канал, а там такой [MASK700], что сразу захотелось всё дописать.
sentence_in_context_gloss: I opened an old channel, and there was such a stale abandoned feeling there that I immediately wanted to finish everything.
paragraph_in_context: Сегодня полез разгребать закладки и наткнулся на свой прошлогодний мини-проект. Код недописан, в чате тишина с марта, а удалить рука не поднимается. Самое точное слово для этого состояния — [MASK700]. Вроде уже не нужно, но висит в голове и царапает.
paragraph_in_context_gloss: Today I went to sort through my bookmarks and stumbled onto my mini-project from last year. The code is unfinished, the chat has been silent since March, and I can't bring myself to delete it. The most accurate word for this feeling is brosnyak. It’s like I don’t need it anymore, but it hangs in my head and scratches at me.
